scenes.headline: How Zephon keeps the global batch fixed
scenes.sub: Lanes, not ranks: the same data on any GPU count.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kilter! Resume training on a different number of GPUs, and most loaders feed different data. Zephon doesn't.

scenes.text: Split the stream into a fixed number of lanes, each with its own packing and shuffle state, and let GPUs own lanes in blocks.
scenes.say: The idea: a fixed number of lanes, each with its own state, owned by GPUs in blocks.

left.title: Rank-sharded loader
items: Each GPU takes every G-th document
Each GPU packs its own rows
Change the GPU count, change the batch
left.say: A usual loader deals documents to GPUs, each packing its own rows. Change the GPU count, and the rows change.

right.title: Zephon lanes
items: Lanes own documents and packing state
Change the GPU count, same batch
right.say: Zephon deals documents to lanes. A GPU only picks where a lane runs.

scenes.title: From chunks to a global batch

steps.say: A work source plans chunks of sample pointers, and a seeded shuffle deals them to lanes.
Each lane tokenizes, packs and shuffles with its own bins and buffers.
GPUs own lanes in blocks. Sixty-four lanes on sixteen GPUs is four each.
Every step takes the same slice from every lane.

scenes.title: Two rules
scenes.text: G divides L, and L divides N / m

parts.note: every GPU owns the same number of lanes
parts.say: The GPU count divides the lane count, so every GPU owns the same number.

parts.note: every lane gives whole microbatches each step
parts.say: The lanes divide the step's microbatches, so each lane gives whole ones.

scenes.label: the only lane count that fits 8 to 64 GPUs here
scenes.note: 448 sequences, 7 per microbatch: 64 microbatches a step
scenes.say: In the paper's run a step is sixty-four microbatches, so only sixty-four lanes fits eight to sixty-four GPUs.

scenes.title: Checkpoint by replay
scenes.say: Resuming needs the packing state, which Zephon never saves.

items.say: It saves a cursor per lane, plus the chunks still in flight.
Every few chunks, a flush empties and resets every bin.
On resume it replays from the last flush, rebuilding the bins.
Then it drops what was delivered.

steps.say: With a standard loader, resumed runs split after the fault, and the hashes turn red.
With Zephon, one curve carries on, and every hash matches.

scenes.text: Zephon fixes the data, not the arithmetic: identical batches can still sum in a different order.
scenes.say: Zephon fixes the data, not the arithmetic. Summed over more GPUs, the same batch rounds a little differently.

recap: Lanes carry the data and its state
The GPU count must divide the lanes
scenes.say: Lanes carry the data. GPUs just run them.
